issue.title: Allow sase monitor start -J/--join with -f prepared completion (stage-diagnostics mirroring + join-time fingerprint guard)

task_type_fields.proposal:
Allow `sase monitor start -J/--join RUN` together with `-f/--completion <ref>`, so an escalated verification run can be finished by a prepared-completion monitor instead of only a `-n/--next` follow-up.

Epic sase-1cx (plan:202609/tool_run_escalation.md, phase monitor-join / sase-1cx.5) shipped `-J` and deliberately refuses `-f` with it in v1 (exit 2, pointing at `-n/--next`). Two pieces are needed to lift that refusal safely (from sase-1cx.5 note #1 and the plan's monitor-join step 7):

1. **Stage-diagnostics mirroring.** The hidden `sase tool _join` worker (src/sase/tool/join_worker.py) streams the joined run's output of record and exit into the monitor log, but it does not mirror the run's stage diagnostics into `SASE_MONITOR_DIAGNOSTICS_DIR`. The prepared-completion `pass` gate checks `required_stages` (sase-core `continuation/completion_eval.rs`), so without mirroring a joined run can never satisfy it.
2. **Join-time workspace fingerprint guard.** The frozen verification command in a prepared intent must still describe the run being joined: refuse the join (or the completion) unless the workspace fingerprint at join time equals the run's recorded `fingerprint_before`.

Then drop the `-f` refusal in src/sase/main/monitor/start.py, update `docs/monitors.md` / `docs/tool.md`, and change the `sase_final` skill source note that currently says an escalated check is finished with `-J ... -n`.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: Explicitly a non-goal of epic sase-1cx ("`-f` prepared completion with `--join`") and proposed as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP by phase sase-1cx.5; it crosses the sase-core completion-evaluation boundary and needs its own design, so it was not folded into the epic's landing.

issue.creation_reason: Epic sase-1cx shipped -J but refuses -f with it in v1; phase sase-1cx.5 proposed lifting that once the joiner mirrors stage diagnostics and a fingerprint guard exists, and the epic's landing plan lists it as an expected follow-up.
